defects.source_says: EO 11727 Sec. 6: 'This order shall be effective as of July 1, 1973.' The claim's own first_end for items (6) and (7) (sec1-6, sec1-7) and its source_notes treat 1973-07-01 as the effective date of the same Sec. 4 deletion and 1973-07-06 only as the alternative reading. The event's effective_date contradicts its own mechanism string and the item clause ends, so the claim gives two different effective dates for one amendment.

reasoning: The corrected dates now agree with the sources: EO 11768 Sec. 4 supersedes EO 11708 as amended on 1974-02-20, EO 11727 deletes items (6) and (7) effective as of 1973-07-01, EO 11715 deletes Sec. 2 item (8) on 1973-04-24, and Sec. 3 performed the partial revocation of EO 11248 on 1973-03-23. Identity, the 25-clause inventory, the search for an earlier end, the handling of the OFR 'Superseded by' note and the savings (EO 11768 Sec. 3 saves appointments only) all check. One defect remains, held to the same standard as the blind review: the EO 11727 later event on Section 1 is dated 1973-07-06. That contradicts the event's own mechanism text, EO 11727 Sec. 6, and the claim's own 1973-07-01 ends for items (6) and (7). The defect is internally inconsistent and does not change the whole-order end; it was also present, unflagged, in the planted version. A note that is not a defect: the original_operative_text for sec2-3 includes the page footer and the next page header (verbatim span, non-operative).
